whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Data Architect exam for?

personas.label: Data Engineers
personas.description: Professionals who manage large-scale data pipelines, ETL processes, and data quality initiatives on the Salesforce Platform.

personas.label: Enterprise Architects
personas.description: Architects responsible for master data management strategies, data governance, and cross-system data consistency.

personas.label: Senior Developers
personas.description: Developers who design data models, write Bulk API integrations, and optimize SOQL queries for high-volume orgs.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Data Architect Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Platform Data Architect exam covers data modeling, master data management, Salesforce data management, governance, large data volumes, and migration. Preparation should include the official objectives and the design trade-offs relevant to each domain.
bullets: 60 scored questions plus up to five unscored questions.
105 minutes and a 58% passing score, according to Salesforce's exam guide.
Six weighted domains cover data modeling, MDM, Salesforce data management, governance, large data volumes, and migration.
Exam fee: US$400; retake fee: US$200, plus applicable taxes. Prerequisite: none.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Book the exam when you can explain skinny tables vs. custom indexes from memory, diagram a multi-system migration load order, and choose the right MDM pattern for a given scenario.

examFormat.heading: Data Architect Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Use the published exam objectives to guide preparation across the six weighted domains; practice explaining the trade-offs among appropriate data architecture options.
bestWayToPass: Know your LDV toolkit: Skinny tables, custom indexes, Async SOQL, Big Objects, and archiving strategies — know exactly when each applies and what it costs.
Master the migration sequence: Understand parent-before-child load order, external ID upsert, Bulk API 2.0 limits, and rollback strategies for failed loads.
Study MDM patterns: Compare approaches for golden records, attribute survivorship, data consolidation, and traceability.
Review data governance: Consider privacy, classification, protection, stewardship, and enterprise governance requirements.

expertInsight: Use Salesforce's published exam objectives as the study scope. For large-data-volume and migration topics, compare design options against the stated access patterns, operational needs, and data-management requirements; do not assume one technique fits every scenario.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests data modeling, large data volume strategies, and migration architecture on the Salesforce Platform. You’ll need to know when to use Big Objects, skinny tables, custom indexes, and MDM patterns for enterprise-scale orgs.

keyConcepts.h2: Data Architect: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Data Modeling: Objects, Relationships, and Big Objects
blocks.body: Compare standard and custom objects, external objects, and big objects against the required data model and access patterns. Big Object SOQL queries are constrained by the big object's index fields. Platform Events provide a schema-defined event mechanism. These topics align with the published data-model and large-data-volume objectives.

blocks.heading: Master Data Management and Deduplication
blocks.body: MDM design considers golden records, attribute survivorship, consolidation of source data, and traceability. Salesforce Matching Rules identify possible duplicates; Duplicate Rules specify how matching records are handled. External IDs can support upsert and cross-system record matching. These topics align with the published MDM objectives.

blocks.heading: Data Migration: Bulk API and Integration Patterns
blocks.body: Bulk API 2.0 is an asynchronous option for ingesting and querying large data sets; it manages ingest batches automatically. Data Loader supports SOAP, Bulk API, and Bulk API 2.0, with the API selected through its settings rather than a fixed 200-record automatic threshold. Choose a loading approach based on data volume, transformations, latency, and operational requirements.

blocks.heading: Data Quality and Governance
blocks.body: Data governance covers identifying, classifying, and protecting personal and sensitive information, as well as enterprise governance practices. Validation Rules, Duplicate Rules, Matching Rules, and field-history features are platform tools to evaluate against the organization's data-quality, privacy, and audit requirements.

blocks.heading: Large Data Volumes: Performance and Archiving
blocks.body: Large Data Volume (LDV) design weighs model scalability and query performance against archiving, purging, and virtualized data options. Salesforce's query optimizer decides whether an index is useful for a query; custom indexes and skinny tables address different performance needs. Use Salesforce's current platform guidance when assessing a specific workload.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Data Architect Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Data Architect exam tests expertise in designing Salesforce data models, managing data quality, and planning data migration. Focus on relationship types, storage limits, archiving strategies, and master data management.

blocks.heading: Advanced Data Modeling
blocks.body: Know when to use lookup, **master-detail**, hierarchical (self-referential), and external relationships. Understand **junction objects**, indirect lookup fields, and how relationship type affects roll-up summaries, cascade delete, and record access.

blocks.heading: Large Data Volume (LDV) Strategies
blocks.body: Know how to handle LDV: skinny tables, custom indexes, selective queries, division archiving, and big objects. Understand what causes a full table scan and how to prevent query timeouts.

blocks.heading: Data Quality & Duplicate Management
blocks.body: Know **Duplicate Rules**, Matching Rules, and how they interact. Understand how to use Data.com clean rules (legacy knowledge), field validation, and data stewardship processes for ongoing data quality.

blocks.heading: Data Migration Architecture
blocks.body: Plan migration using **external IDs** (upsert strategy), parent-before-child load order, and the appropriate API (**Bulk API** for volume, REST for real-time). Understand data validation and rollback strategies.

blocks.heading: Master Data Management
blocks.body: Know MDM patterns: Registry, Consolidation, and Coexistence. Understand how to implement a golden record strategy, handle conflicting records, and synchronize master data across systems.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the primary focus of a Platform Data Architect?
options: Designing sound, scalable, high-performing solutions for enterprise data management on the Salesforce Platform
sampleQuestions.explanation: Platform Data Architects design scalable, high-performing data solutions on the Salesforce Platform.
whyWrong: 'Only UI' undersells the Data Architect's actual focus, which is scalable enterprise data management, not interface design.
Email is unrelated to the Data Architect's core data management focus.
Slack is unrelated to the Data Architect's core data management focus.

sampleQuestions.question: Which consideration is critical when designing for large data volumes?
options: Governor limits, indexing, and query optimization
sampleQuestions.explanation: Large data volumes require attention to governor limits, indexing, and query optimization.
whyWrong: 'Only field count' oversimplifies LDV design, which centers on governor limits, indexing, and query optimization, not just field count.
'Only page layout' is a UI concern, unrelated to large data volume performance design.
'Only reports' is a display concern, unrelated to the underlying data volume performance strategy.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of skinny tables in Salesforce?
options: To optimize reporting by reducing joins for large datasets
sampleQuestions.explanation: Skinny tables are denormalized tables that can improve report performance.
whyWrong: Skinny tables aren't for storing images — that's unrelated to their reporting-performance purpose.
Skinny tables aren't for sending emails — that's unrelated to their function.
Skinny tables aren't for CPQ configuration — that's unrelated to their function.

sampleQuestions.question: Which relationship type should be used when the child must always belong to a parent?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Master-Detail enforces ownership and cascade delete; child cannot exist without parent.
whyWrong: Lookup relationships allow the child to exist without a parent — the opposite of what's needed here.
External Lookup connects to external system data, not a strict parent-child requirement.
Indirect Lookup is used for external objects matching on specific fields, not enforcing a required parent.

sampleQuestions.question: What does data archiving strategy involve?
options: Moving historical data off-platform or to Big Objects while keeping access patterns in mind
sampleQuestions.explanation: Archiving involves moving historical data while preserving access and compliance.
whyWrong: 'Only backup' undersells archiving strategy, which also considers ongoing access patterns, not just backup.
'Only delete' misrepresents archiving, which is about retaining accessible historical data, not deleting it outright.
'Only export' undersells archiving strategy, which is broader than simple export.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Big Object in Salesforce?
options: A custom object optimized for high-volume, append-only historical data
sampleQuestions.explanation: Big Objects store high-volume historical data with optimized query patterns.
whyWrong: A standard object doesn't have Big Object's specific high-volume, append-only optimization.
A report type is a display configuration, not a data storage mechanism like Big Objects.
A dashboard visualizes data — it isn't itself a storage mechanism.

sampleQuestions.question: Which indexing strategy improves SOQL performance?
options: Custom indexes on frequently filtered fields and standard indexed fields
sampleQuestions.explanation: Custom indexes on filtered fields improve query performance.
whyWrong: 'No indexing' contradicts the fact that indexing strategy directly improves SOQL performance.
Indexing every field is impractical and doesn't reflect the targeted, selective indexing approach that's actually recommended.
Limiting indexing only to formula fields ignores the broader set of frequently-filtered fields that benefit from indexing.

sampleQuestions.question: What does data migration planning include?
options: Extract, transform, load (ETL), validation, and rollback strategy
sampleQuestions.explanation: Migration includes ETL, validation, and rollback planning.
whyWrong: 'Only export' undersells migration planning, which includes transformation, validation, and rollback too.
'Only import' undersells migration planning, which includes the full ETL and validation process, not just import.
'Only backup' misrepresents migration planning, which is about moving and transforming data, not backing it up.

sampleQuestions.question: Which relationship type allows a child to exist without a parent?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lookup allows optional parent; child can exist independently.
whyWrong: Master-Detail relationships require the parent to exist — the opposite of what's being asked.
Junction objects use two master-detail relationships, so children still require parents in that structure.
External Lookup connects to external system records, which is a different scenario from a standard child-without-parent case.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a soft delete strategy?
options: To mark records as deleted while retaining for compliance or recovery
sampleQuestions.explanation: Soft delete preserves data with a deleted flag for compliance.
whyWrong: Permanently removing data is the opposite of a soft delete, which retains records.
'To export data only' misrepresents the purpose of soft delete, which is about retention, not export.
'To archive only' undersells soft delete's specific purpose around compliance and recovery.

sampleQuestions.question: Which governor limit affects bulk SOQL in triggers?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Synchronous limit is 100 SOQL queries per transaction.
whyWrong: 'No limit' contradicts the fact that Salesforce enforces a specific SOQL governor limit.
'Unlimited' contradicts the fact that a specific limit (100 for synchronous) exists.
'50 queries' understates the actual synchronous SOQL limit of 100.

sampleQuestions.question: What does master data management (MDM) address?
options: Single source of truth, deduplication, and data quality
sampleQuestions.explanation: MDM ensures consistent, clean master data across systems.
whyWrong: 'Only reporting' undersells MDM, which is about data quality and single source of truth, not just reporting.
'Only archiving' misrepresents MDM's actual focus on deduplication and data quality.
'Only migration' misrepresents MDM's actual focus on ongoing data quality, not just migration.

sampleQuestions.question: Which data type supports high-volume, append-only use cases?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Big Objects are designed for append-only, high-volume data.
whyWrong: A standard object doesn't have the append-only, high-volume optimization Big Objects provide.
A custom object with triggers doesn't scale the same way as the purpose-built Big Object architecture.
External objects connect to external data — they aren't the native high-volume append-only storage type being asked about.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the benefit of using External Objects?
options: To query external data without replicating it into Salesforce
sampleQuestions.explanation: External Objects enable querying external systems in real time.
whyWrong: External Objects don't replace custom objects — they serve a different purpose (querying without replication).
External Objects aren't specifically an archiving mechanism — that's a different, distinct use case.
External Objects aren't a reporting tool — their benefit is querying live external data without replication.

sampleQuestions.question: Which consideration applies when designing for data volume growth?
options: Archiving strategy, indexing, and query selectivity
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data growth requires archiving, indexing, and selective queries.
whyWrong: Ignoring limits contradicts the core consideration needed when designing for data volume growth.
'Only backup' undersells the broader set of considerations (archiving, indexing, query selectivity) needed for growth planning.
'Only export' undersells the broader set of considerations needed for data volume growth planning.
